title: Lines Composed a Few Miles above Tintern Abbey, on Revisiting the Banks of the Wye during a Tour, July 13, 1798

access.edition_or_version: First published 1798 in the first edition of Lyrical Ballads (publication year verified 2026-09-24); public-domain text. Claims use whole-poem description, not line numbers.

tone_mechanisms_observed: recollected-in-tranquillity composition: sensation remembered in the absence of the scene, feeding present thought
dated revisits: the poem's title pins the reflective stance to a specific occasion (July 13, 1798)
three stacked time layers in one utterance — earlier visit, later visit, present recollection
earlier selves corrected rather than idealized — the anti-nostalgia use of memory
mechanics.point_of_view: First-person speaker revisiting a remembered landscape, observing his own changing relation to it across time.
mechanics.tense_and_structure: Subordinate past-tense frames hold a present-tense core: grammatical embodiment of memory feeding the present; the title supplies the date that keeps reflection from floating.
mechanics.rhythm_and_cadence: Blank-verse periods with caesura pauses marking the turn between time layers; reflective pacing slows the middle of the poem.
mechanics.psychic_distance: Medium-close, but diachronic: the speaker regards his own younger selves from the standpoint of the present — self-distance produced by time, not pronoun.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Landscape as anchor for moral memory; similes that compare states of mind across years rather than decorate scenery.
mechanics.copyright_note: Public domain. Described by technique only; no lines reproduced.
